ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and periodic screening of the founder, foundation council members, protector, beneficiary, and any controlling settlor against UN Consolidated Sanctions Lists, OFAC SDN List, EU restrictive measures, and Panama's national screening databases; enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP or family/close associate of a PEP, including written source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; any sanctions hit must be immediately escalated to the compliance officer and, where legally required, reported to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sede Electrónica / Oficina Electrónica
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official registry language is Spanish; names may be submitted using the Latin alphabet, but the foundation's legal form or a descriptive equivalent must be recognizable in Spanish; transliteration into Spanish alphabet is required for non-Roman script names, and the registered name must not create phonetic identity or deceptive similarity with an existing registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection or objection, the applicant or registered agent must file a written reconsideration request with the Registro Público de Panamá before the expiry of the administrative filing window, ordinarily within five business days of notification; the request must attach a comparative registry search report demonstrating distinguishability; if reconsideration is denied, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal before the relevant registry appeals body and ultimately judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. A rejected name may be resubmitted with corrected distinguishing elements or an alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible for the statutory registered office of a Private Interest Foundation, provided a licensed resident agent maintains a physical address in Panama for service of process and official communications. A purely virtual address without a resident agent relationship is not acceptable. For operational e-commerce activity through Etsy and Stripe, the foundation should also provide a substantive business address or clearly documented independent agent relationship to satisfy payment processor and financial intermediary due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 5% for this low-risk novelty merchandise industry in the first operating year; the likelihood increases to approximately 15-20% if the UBO regime is non-compliant, PEP exposure exists, or payment processor 'high-risk' flags arise. Unannounced inspections are uncommon for private foundations but may occur through regulatory verification of registered agent records rather than physical site visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley No. 13 de 2017; Articles 1-39 (creation, endowment, Foundation Council, protector, registration and certification).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter / Founding Act) submitted for inscription in the Registro de Fundaciones
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum endowment of US$10,000 (or its equivalent in lawful assets, cash, or obligations convertible to cash) required by Article 18 of Law No. 25 of 1995. No escrow account is mandated by statute; the endowment may be represented by a subscription credited to the foundation's corporate bank account in Panama, with the registered agent attesting to the contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 001. At a meeting of the Foundation Council of [Fundación], held in Panama City, it is unanimously RESOLVED: (1) The initial endowment of US$10,000, contributed by the founder, is accepted as fully subscribed and shall be credited to the foundation's corporate account. (2) The registered office is established at [Registered Agent], Panama City, Republic of Panama, which shall serve as legal domicile and registered agent. (3) [President], [Secretary], and [Treasurer] are appointed as officers of the Foundation Council for the term prescribed by the Charter. (4) The President is authorized to open bank accounts, execute manufacturing leases, and apply for all municipal, environmental, and fire-safety permits. (5) This resolution shall be filed with the Public Registry and remain in full force.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name-search application (solicitud de búsqueda de nombre) through the licensed registered agent. The proposed foundation name must contain or be followed by the word 'Fundación' or 'F.I.P.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Panamanian entity. The registry issues a Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre confirming availability.
required_dossiers: Signed application letter from the registered agent
Proposed foundation name and object (manufacture and polishing of enamel lapel pins)
Power of attorney or engagement letter of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, the registered agent files a name-change request (renuncia y cambio de nombre) or submits a revised name with a new search certificate before notarization; no registry penalty applies if corrected prior to presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Private Interest Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (licensed Panamanian Notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter) including the foundation name, object (die-struck brass cloisonné polishing of novelty enamel badges), minimum endowment of US$10,000, Foundation Council members, registered agent domicile, beneficiary provisions, and dissolution rules. Execute the instrument before a Panamanian notary with the registered agent and founder present, obtaining the notary's protocol number.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva)
Client due diligence and source-of-funds questionnaires
Registered agent acceptance letter
Shareholder or founder identification documents (passport / ID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any drafting defect or clerical error is cured by executing a notarized rectification instrument (aclaración) before the same or another notary, which is then attached to the principal Charter for registry presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Presentation and Inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered attorney files the notarized Foundation Charter together with the name search certificate, the registered agent's qualification certificate, and the payment of the government filing fee (approximately US$150). The Registry reviews the instrument for statutory compliance and assigns a folio number upon inscription.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (original and copies)
Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre
Registered agent qualification certificate (idóneo attorney certificate)
Government fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues observaciones (e.g., missing endowment clause or defective agent acceptance), the registered attorney files a written respuesta and, if necessary, a notarized addendum, within the correction term; the instrument is then re-presented for inscription without loss of priority if cured timely.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registration Certificate and Certified Copy of the Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina de Certificaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request the official certified copy (copia certificada) of the inscribed Foundation Charter and the Certificado de Fundación (Personal Certificate) evidencing the foundation's legal existence, folio number, and registration date. These certified documents constitute the legal personality proof for banks and authorities.
required_dossiers: Registry folio number assigned upon inscription
Certified copy request form signed by registered agent
Payment of certification fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified copy contains transcription errors or omits clauses, file a written solicitud de corrección with the Registry's certification office; a corrected certified copy is issued normally within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the General Directorate of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation with the DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). Since the foundation will conduct commercial manufacturing and sales activity in Panama, register for Corporate Income Tax under the territorial tax rules, as well as for the complementary tax scheme, and obtain the relevant taxpayer obligations. The DGI requires presentation of the certified Charter and registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter from the Public Registry
Certificado de Fundación (registration certificate)
RUC application form (Formulario RUC DGI-01)
Identification of legal representative and registered agent
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries incomplete data or discrepancies, submit a Formulario de Actualización de Datos (data update form) and supporting certified documents; a corrective filing is processed before the tax registry window without penalty if filed prior to the first tax period deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Activation of Payment Gateways
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá-regulated banking entity (e.g., Banco Nacional de Panamá or licensed private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certified Foundation Charter, Certificado de Fundación, RUC certificate, and Foundation Council Resolution No. 001 to open a corporate USD account in the foundation's name. After account opening, activate the target payment rails, Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe, using the foundation's bank account and tax registration details. The institution applies standard Low-Risk KYC/AML due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certified Foundation Charter and Certificado de Fundación
RUC certificate issued by DGI
Foundation Council Resolution appointing officers and authorizing bank signatories
Passport or ID of legal representative and beneficial owner
Bank reference or source-of-funds affidavit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, present a notarized source-of-funds affidavit, a CPA-reviewed financial statement of the founder, or a legal opinion from a Panamanian attorney; if rejected, apply to an alternate licensed bank under the foundation's registered name.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía Municipal de Panamá – Dirección de Administración de Rentas (Municipal Revenue Authority) and the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (for industrial registration where applicable)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación y Patente Municipal (Municipal Business Operating License and Industrial Patent)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Información Ambiental, Departamento de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II – Registro de Impacto Ambiental under Law 41 of 1998 and Executive Decree No. 57 of 2015; a small enamel badge manufacturing and polishing workshop with light metalwork and chemical polishing of brass blanks may be screened as Category I (exempt) or Category II (registration) depending on installed capacity, effluents, and chemicals used, subject to MiAMBIENTE's site-based classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to public sewers must meet the Panamanian Norma de Calidad Ambiental para Descarga de Aguas Residuales (Ministerial Resolution No. 1000 of 2010); air emissions and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from enameling ovens must comply with the COPANIT atmospheric norms under Decree No. 2 of 1982; enameling sludge, metal filings, and spent chemicals must be classified under Ley 41 de 1998 and disposed of at MiAMBIENTE-registered facilities, with waste manifests retained for five years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Seguridad y Protección Contra Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá based on inspection of enameling ovens, chemical storage, and evacuation routes; structural load and electrical installation inspection certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian engineer and accepted by the Municipality of Panama; occupational health and workplace safety clearance from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 24 de 1977 and the General Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, including ventilation, personal protective equipment, and chemical hazard labeling.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); unified digital portal: SITIO (Sistema Integrado de Información Tributaria), https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa; customs export control: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), https://www.ana.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-established Private Interest Foundation (PIF, Ley 25 de 12 June 1995) must obtain a RUC/NIT taxpayer identifier before executing any Panamanian-source supply. Procedure: (1) register the foundation charter (acta constitutiva) in the Public Registry and maintain a resident agent; (2) file the RUC registration via SITIO with certified charter, registry enrollment certificate, and legal representative credentials; (3) update the expediente with CIIU/ISIC activity code 3240, enroll in ITBMS, and request exporter status; (4) obtain the Registro de Exportadores enrollment (MICI) and register in the SADA customs system for outward clearance; (5) secure a DGI digital certificate for electronic invoicing (SFE). Non-resident ownership is unrestricted; no physical presence in Panama is required beyond the resident agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope – the PIF is a distinct legal person taxed at entity level (25% ISR) only on income sourced in Panama (Código Fiscal Art. 712 et seq.); foreign-source income, foreign assets, and offshore accounts fall outside the Panamanian tax net. The PIF is statutorily exempt from Panamanian taxes on offshore patrimonial income; Panamanian-source commercial income (e.g., local sales of hard enamel lapel pins) is taxed at 25% with no pass-through to founders or beneficiaries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or disregarded-entity election exists in Panamanian law; classification follows civil-law form. Available elections: (i) simplified small-taxpayer presumptive regime (Ley 66 de 2022) for merchants with annual gross income up to approximately B/. 36,000, generally unavailable to entity-form taxpayers; (ii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) preferential regime under Ley 41 de 2007 (5% ISR) for qualifying regional operations; (iii) manufacturing/export incentive regimes administered by MICI applicable to pin production and export; (iv) economic substance compliance under Ley 70 de 2019 for PIFs conducting relevant activities (distribution/service centers), requiring annual substance filings where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (VAT), Ley 33 de 2011, Código Fiscal Arts. 1057-A et seq.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold: any person performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS prior to the first taxable event (Código Fiscal Art. 1132-A). A simplified presumptive regime covers small natural-person merchants with annual gross income up to approximately B/. 36,000 (Ley 66 de 2022); PIFs with commercial turnover remain in the general regime. Export supplies are 0% rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under Decreto Ejecutivo 59 de 26 July 2019: all ITBMS registrants must issue e-invoices via the DGI SFE (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica) through DGI-certified software, the free SITIO web issuer, or API-integrated systems; each invoice is transmitted to DGI before delivery and receives a unique Código de Operación plus a DGI-validated QR fiscal seal; serial ranges for issuance are pre-authorized by DGI; alcoholic beverages and cigarettes require additional physical fiscal stamps (precintos). DGI cross-references e-invoice data with SADA export declarations and SITIO returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (including hard enamel lapel pins) are zero-rated under Código Fiscal Art. 1057-T. Requirements: (i) physical departure of goods from Panamanian customs territory evidenced by an accepted SADA/DUA export declaration; (ii) the PIF is the registered exporter with MICI; (iii) sale is to a foreign buyer, with payment sourced from non-resident payers (Etsy/Direct Pay or Stripe payout records acceptable as supplementary evidence); (iv) purchase, transport, and customs documentation are retained; (v) for services, performance and effective use occur outside Panama. Input ITBMS is creditable and excess balances may be refunded quarterly (devolución de saldo a favor) via SITIO.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA) with ANA SADA acceptance and exit stamp
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier consignment note evidencing foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT confirmation of export proceeds; Etsy/Stripe payout reconciliation reports where banking certificates are unavailable
Commercial invoice and packing list (zero-rated line)
Foundation records evidencing buyer, Incoterms, and cost of goods sold
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA cross-match export declarations, e-invoices, and foreign-exchange records. Unsupported or fictitious zero-rating claims trigger: (i) reassessment of ITBMS at 7% plus monthly surcharge and inflation adjustment; (ii) fines of 100%–200% of the omitted tax under Código Fiscal Arts. 1067 and 1139-B; (iii) retrospective clawback of refunded input credits with statutory interest; (iv) suspension or removal from the Registro de Exportadores and cancellation of e-invoice authorizations; (v) criminal tax fraud liability for directors/founders under Código Penal Arts. 583–586, with imprisonment; the DGI limitation period is 5 years from the filing date, extended in cases of fraud or concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: None - fully dollarized economy; bank supervision and AML/CFT oversight is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Banco Nacional de Panamá functions as the fiscal agent and USD clearing intermediary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The balboa circulates only as non-existent paper money; USD banknotes are legal tender. Both current-account and capital-account conversion are unrestricted. There is no exchange-control regime, no foreign-investment registration requirement for PIF contributions, and no hurdle to profit, dividend, or endowment remittance. Territorial taxation further eliminates attributable taxation on offshore-source receipts from a Panama Private Interest Foundation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion obligation exists under Panamanian law. Export proceeds in any currency may be retained in domestically chartered or foreign bank accounts without mandatory conversion to USD. AML reporting thresholds apply only through SBP-regulated banks under the Beneficial Ownership Law 23 of 2015.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. Panama has no dedicated EMI licensing regime at the same operational ease as EU PSD2; SBP-regulated fintechs exist, but offshore digital EMIs, particularly US neobanks and UK e-money houses, routinely refuse a Panama PIF as a customer class due to enhanced due-diligence opacity regarding protectors and beneficiaries. Open banking is not yet ubiquitous, and most practical onboarding still requires a correspondent bank relationship with a SBP-licensed physical institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: First-time tier-1 commercial-bank onboarding generally mandates physical appearance of at least one foundation council member or an expressly appointed signatory before a compliance officer. Remote opening is only possible through private-banking intermediation after pre-screening; it is not a statutory right, and the waiver must be documented in compliance-committee minutes to survive SBP review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity due to the foundation council, protector, and designated beneficiaries beneath Private Interest Foundation Law 25 of 1995.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Acto Constitutivo, RUC (tax ID) of the PIF, recent good-standing certificate from the Registro Público de Panamá, appointment of the registered agent, current foundation council register, and a sworn declaration of the source of the initial endowment and ongoing funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative-scoring sanctions or PEP resonance from a non-resident director or beneficiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports of all council members and beneficiaries; criminal-record certificates from each country of residence; three independent bank-reference letters from the preceding five years; source-of-wealth report; and a sanctions-screening result dated within thirty days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-expectation mismatch for ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339999 merchandise sales through Etsy and Stripe without documentary proof of commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier contracts for die-struck brass blanks, cloisonné enamel supply-chain invoices, purchase orders, packing lists, incoterms agreements, Etsy payout analytics, and Stripe merchant history to demonstrate a genuine low-risk enamel-lapel-pin commercial flow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound endowment and working-capital injections must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with precise beneficiary identification (PIF legal name, the university or private foundation account, RUC number, and registered-agent reference). As Panama does not enforce exchange controls, the SWIFT PURP field may carry a transparent descriptor such as 'ENDOWMENT-CAPITAL' or 'FOUNDATION-IN-KIND'; no mandatory Central Bank registration approval applies. Correspondent banks in the United States require the PIF's name to exactly match the registry entry to avoid return-advice fees.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of raw-material purchases uses SWIFT MT103 over correspondent USD clearing rails (Fedwire and CHIPS); commercial letters of credit are operated via MT700 issuing banks after compliance clearance. Regular Etsy/Stripe payouts run as card-network batches, with the USD air-gap eliminated because Panamanian accounts are held in the same currency; the PIF's operational account acts as the final clearing anchor before bank transfers to Chinese brass-pin manufacturers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH deliverable forwards for mainland-China enamel pin supplier settlements
USD/MXN non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for regional trade counterparties
USD/COP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for South-American sales realization
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps for EU-based Etsy Marketplaces
OTC FX options executed through SBP-licensed banks only

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee for Private Interest Foundation (annual foundation tax under Law 25 of 1995, as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama, through licensed Panamanian registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before May 31; the fee applies for the full calendar year and is not prorated after initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late monthly surcharge of USD 10 per month, capped at USD 100; a two-year unpaid balance blocks certificates of good standing and may lead to administrative suspension or cancellation of the foundation registration by the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Owner Declaration (RBF annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Beneficial Owner Registry under the Panamanian final beneficial owner reporting regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before May 31; any material change in beneficial ownership, Foundation Council membership, or beneficiary rights must be updated within 30 calendar days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines in the range of USD 500 to USD 5,000 under the beneficial-owner regulation; arrears prevent issuance of good-standing certificates and may freeze registry amendments and asset disposition instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered agent annual continuity confirmation and statutory register audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; confirmation is retained by the licensed resident agent in the statutory registers, with any notarized change of agent or registered office filed at the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed government due date; must be completed no later than May 31 so that the resident agent can certify the Foundation Council, beneficiary register, minute book, and accounting records before the annual fee and beneficial-owner filing are submitted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the required Panamanian registered agent and current statutory registers can invalidate registry certificates, make acts in the foundation subject to judicial challenge, and expose Foundation Council members and the resident agent to civil liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Panamanian Law 25 of 1995. A Private Interest Foundation is not subject to a statutory audit based on revenue, assets, employees, or registered capital. An independent audit is required only when the foundation charter or rules mandate an auditor, when a court or protector orders one, or when a bank, payment processor, or acquiring platform such as Etsy or Stripe makes an audit or review a condition of continued business relationship.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No publicly mandated accounting framework for a non-public Panamanian Private Interest Foundation. Where financial statements are prepared for the Foundation Council, banks, or payment platforms, IFRS or IFRS for SMEs is the practical professional benchmark; Panamanian local GAAP is also acceptable if applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Panama Private Interest Foundation has no share register. Changes in beneficiary rights are recorded through notarized amendments to the foundation charter or through resolutions of the Foundation Council. The registered agent must obtain and preserve beneficial-owner due-diligence information and must submit an annual final beneficial-owner declaration to the Registro Público de Panamá before each May 31. The declaration reconfirms that no undisclosed beneficiary or Foundation Council member has been added, and any appointment, resignation, replacement, or transfer of rights occurring during the year is reflected in the statutory minute book, the private beneficiary register, and the next annual declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,200 per year for standard licensed resident agent and registered office services; full-service administration with domicile, bookkeeping, and final beneficial-owner filing typically ranges from USD 1,000 to USD 2,500 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No mandatory audit; where an independent audit is voluntarily adopted or required by Etsy, Stripe, or a bank, a compact e-commerce audit by a Panamanian CPA firm is typically USD 1,500 - USD 5,000, while a review or compilation engagement may be USD 600 - USD 1,800

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Código Fiscal Art. 699) on net taxable income derived from Panamanian source; the territorial system excludes foreign-source business income, foreign dividends and gains on foreign intellectual property from the tax base.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for Private Interest Foundations (PIFs). The effective tax rate on pure Panamanian-source commercial manufacturing income is 25%; however, income from export sales may benefit from VAT zero-rating, and income derived from assets located or activities performed outside Panama is outside the Panamanian tax net. A PIF that simply holds shares and receives exempt or foreign dividends can achieve 0% Panama corporate income tax.
